wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protection is over filter values sent to one database, not access to a resource; there is no neighbouring or proxy object to authorise
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles, peers or directions; every caller-supplied filter takes the same path
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the flaw is script execution inside a query; the protected property is over the filter value, not over a verb, and the same path serves every operation
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no offset, clamp, unit conversion or normalisation turns the attacker's value into a different bad value on this path
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, token or path parsing is involved in the protected path
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or secret lookup exists on this path

traps.shape: a caller-supplied populate match carries the server-side script operator at the top level, nested in a logical operator, in an array of per-document filters, in a match-function result, or in a virtual populate's match; the guard must recurse through every shape while direct developer-written script queries keep working
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report shows one top-level key, and a check for that key at the two match sites looks complete; the nested logical form, the array of per-document filters, the match-function result and the virtual branch each reach the same query by a different shape.

traps.shape: a caller-supplied populate match carries server-side JavaScript through an aggregation expression's function operator instead of the script key, at the top level, nested in a logical operator, used as an expression operand, or in a virtual populate match
traps.reason_to_dismiss: both advisories name only the script key, and the aggregation-expression form is a legitimate, common operator in a populate filter; a walker that looks for the script key sees nothing, and the expression caster only rewrites its known operator list.

traps.shape: an application that opts into neutralising untrusted filter values still passes a top-level or logically nested script operator through to the database, because the sanitiser wraps object values but never treats the script operator's own key as untrusted
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the sanitiser is documented to wrap nested operator objects in an equality match; a string-valued script operator and a negation container look outside its remit, and it is not on the populate-match path the report leads to.
